passage:
A charity gave solar lanterns to students in a village with unreliable electricity. The lanterns charged during the day and gave light at night.
Students could study without smoky fuel lamps. Families also used them for cooking and walking outside after dark.
However, the program included repair training because broken lanterns would become useless trash without local knowledge.
A student who received a lantern said it did not only give light. It gave time.
The project showed that helpful technology should be designed with maintenance in mind. Giving a tool is not enough. People need the power to keep it working.
